premises: Rapid formation of a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale (e.g., Cr2O3, Al2O3) governs oxidation resistance.
Sufficient concentration of protective oxide-forming elements (Cr, Al) is necessary.
A refined nanocrystalline microstructure provides abundant grain boundaries.
These grain boundaries act as short-circuit diffusion paths, accelerating transport of protective elements to the surface.
This synergistic effect leads to lower oxidation rates and better mechanical integrity retention compared to coarse-grained alloys.
